result.title: Budgeted Proper Loss Design for Uncertain Decision Thresholds
result.summary: A binary probability estimate may be used by several decision makers with different error costs. Proper scoring rules can emphasize selected probability thresholds, but a single average threshold distribution need not give a good worst-case regret guarantee. We study the choice of a proper loss when the threshold distribution belongs to a finite specified family. Among integrable loss weights with a positive pointwise floor and a fixed total mass, we derive the weight that minimizes the sharp, distribution-free multiplier from surrogate regret to threshold-averaged decision regret. The solution clips a rescaled upper envelope of the threshold densities at the prescribed floor; its normalization is found by a one-dimensional root search. We give proofs of sharpness, optimality, and stability under density misspecification, as well as a limitation for atomic threshold laws. An exact histogram implementation and two synthetic experiments across 20 seeds verify the construction. The optimized multiplier improves over uniform and average-density weights, while fitted-model performance does not improve uniformly. The result is a loss-design guarantee under an explicit budget, rather than a general claim of predictive superiority.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在阈值分布属于指定有限族、损失权重总预算固定的条件下如何选择 proper loss，使「代理遗憾→阈值平均决策遗憾」的最坏情况乘子最小，并给出截断上包络构造、尖锐性与稳定性证明及合成验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预算约束下阈值不确定的决策遗憾」目标可能与 LVR 中 STOP 决策的损失设计与稳健停止规则存在概念联系，可供核查；但论文为纯决策理论、无视觉或多模态状态内容。
